questions.question:
Complete
Mark 0 out of 1
Which resources can be limited by Control Groups (cgroups) in libcontainer?
Select one:
questions.explanation: Cgroups can limit CPU time, memory, block-device I/O rates, and the number of processes in a cgroup. They do not directly impose a disk-capacity quota: the cgroup I/O controller limits bytes per second or I/O operations per second. The source key’s option B says disk space, which is inaccurate. The kernel’s pids.max control sets a hard maximum on the number of processes, so option D is the supported answer after clarifying it as a process-count limit.

optionExplanations.A: Cgroups constrain resources assigned to container processes; they do not set a general resource budget for the Docker daemon.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect as worded: CPU and memory can be limited, but cgroup I/O controls limit I/O rates, not storage capacity (disk space).
optionExplanations.C: Network traffic control is handled by network facilities; this option is not the cgroup resource described here.
optionExplanations.D: Correct after clarification: the pids controller limits the number of processes in the cgroup.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an aim of the Change Management process?

options.text: Standardized methods and procedures are used for efficient and prompt handling of all changes.
All budgets and expenditures are accounted for.
All changes to service assets and configuration items are recorded in the Configuration Management System.

questions.explanation: In ITIL v3, Change Management coordinates changes and controls their risk. questions.question: Which NIST cloud service model gives the consumer the least control over the underlying infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Interpreting “most restrictive” as giving the consumer the least control, SaaS is the answer. In SaaS, the provider runs the application and controls the underlying cloud infrastructure; PaaS gives the consumer control over deployed applications, and IaaS gives more control over operating systems and applications. NIST therefore supports A, not the source key’s PaaS. I have clarified the stem to state the control criterion explicitly.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: SaaS gives consumers the least control over the underlying cloud infrastructure.
optionExplanations.B: IaaS gives consumers control over operating systems, storage, and deployed applications.
optionExplanations.C: CaaS is not one of NIST’s three standard cloud service models listed here.
optionExplanations.D: PaaS allows consumers to deploy and control their applications, so it is less restrictive than SaaS.

questions.question:
Which of the following terms refers to the management and location of cloud
infrastructure.

questions.question: What is a RACI model used for?
questions.explanation: A RACI matrix maps people or roles to tasks using four involvement labels: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed. It makes ownership and communication responsibilities clear. It is not a performance-analysis tool, a configuration-item register, or a service-monitoring system.

optionExplanations.C: Configuration items are recorded in a configuration-management system.
optionExplanations.D: Service monitoring observes service health; RACI assigns involvement and accountability.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is wrong?

options.text: The use of the word “cloud” makes reference to the two essential concepts.
Cloud computing abstracts systems by pooling and sharing resources
Cloud computing is nothing more than the Internet.

questions.explanation: The false statement is C. Internet access is one way to reach cloud services, but cloud computing also involves on-demand provisioning, pooled resources, elasticity, metering, and service and deployment models. NIST explicitly lists resource pooling as a cloud characteristic, so B is broadly consistent with the standard definition. The source’s introductory explanation frames A as abstraction and virtualization. “All of the mentioned” cannot be right because the other statements are not all false.

optionExplanations.A: In the source’s introductory framing, “cloud” refers to abstraction and virtualization; the wording is broad but is not the false statement intended here.
optionExplanations.B: NIST includes resource pooling as a defining cloud characteristic, making this broadly true.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: cloud computing is not merely the Internet; it is a model for provisioned, pooled computing resources with additional characteristics and service/deployment models.
optionExplanations.D: Not correct because the statements are not all false.

files.sourcePdf: IT Infrastructure Management & DevOps/ITIL, DevOps & DCM/Cloud Computing/Cloud Computing.pdf
files.answerEvidenceSummary: Explicit answer marker in the source PDF.

verification.reason: The source prints B as the answer, but NIST defines cloud computing using on-demand network access to pooled resources and several other characteristics; resource pooling is explicitly one of those characteristics, so B is not the false statement as written. The NIST definition also shows cloud computing is more than the Internet alone. The question’s accompanying course explanation identifies abstraction and virtualization as the two introductory concepts referenced by A. Therefore C is the best single false statement and the source key is corrected from B to C.

questions.question: What does lift-and-shift migration refer to in cloud migration?

options.text: Migrating applications with major code changes
Moving applications to the cloud with minimal modification
Rewriting applications to use cloud-native features

questions.explanation: Lift-and-shift, also called rehosting, moves an existing application or workload to cloud infrastructure with little or no code change. The workload runs in a new location but keeps its basic architecture. Rewriting for cloud-native features is refactoring or modernization; copying data for disaster recovery is a separate strategy.

optionExplanations.A: Major code changes are not the defining feature of lift-and-shift.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: the workload is moved with minimal modification or no code changes.
optionExplanations.C: Rewriting the application to use cloud-native services is a refactor/modernization approach.
optionExplanations.D: Replicating data for recovery is not lift-and-shift migration.

questions.question: In the SPEC Benchmark, non-base options are also known as ______ metrics.
questions.explanation: SPEC reports benchmark results using base and peak metrics. Base results follow stricter, more uniform compilation rules; peak results allow greater flexibility for tuning individual benchmarks. Therefore non-base metrics are called peak metrics. “Apex,” “top,” and “lean” are not SPEC metric categories.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: SPEC uses “peak” for its more flexible, optional metric set.
optionExplanations.B: Apex is not the SPEC term.
optionExplanations.C: Top is not the SPEC term.
optionExplanations.D: Lean is not the SPEC term; Jayaswal is part of the source’s book reference.

questions.question: A virtual machine is abstracted from the physical host’s ______.
questions.explanation: A virtual machine behaves like a computer but receives virtualized processor, memory, storage, and device resources through a hypervisor. The hypervisor mediates access to the physical host’s hardware, so the guest is insulated from direct hardware details while still depending on that hardware.

optionExplanations.A: Software runs on or manages the VM; it is not the physical resource being abstracted here.
optionExplanations.B: Hardware is not ‘overlying’ the virtual machine in this relationship.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: the hypervisor abstracts the underlying physical hardware and presents virtual resources.
optionExplanations.D: Software above the VM is not the physical host resource the question describes.

questions.question: A data center wants the virtualization layer to run directly on physical hardware without first loading a general-purpose host operating system. Which hypervisor type fits?
questions.explanation: A Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor runs at the hardware virtualization layer and manages virtual machines without first running as an ordinary application on a general-purpose host OS. A Type 2 hypervisor is hosted by an operating system.

questions.question: In the SPEC Benchmark, non-base options are also known as ______ metrics.
questions.explanation: In SPEC CPU2006 terminology, “peak” is the optional, more aggressively tuned metric, while “base” follows stricter common compilation rules. Thus non-base options are called peak metrics.

questions.question: Which type of network cable transmits digital signals in the form of pulses of light?
questions.explanation: Fiber-optic cable carries information as light pulses in an optical fiber. Coaxial, UTP, and STP carry electrical signals through copper conductors, so they are not the answer.

questions.question: Which command-line tool manages KVM-based VMs?
questions.explanation: `virsh` is the libvirt command-line client for working with virtual machine domains. It can list, start, pause, and shut down VMs, including KVM guests. `top` monitors processes, `nano` edits text, and Docker manages containers.

questions.question: What does the term “elasticity” in cloud computing refer to?

options.text: Both a and c are correct

questions.explanation: Cloud elasticity is the ability to provision more resources when demand rises and release them when demand falls. The question’s “up” and “down” wording is a simplified description of that two-way adjustment.
